name: The Good and the Beautiful Math
line: The Good and the Beautiful Math is daily lessons an adult teaches and grades. In AMP, both happen at every problem.
description: AMP vs The Good and the Beautiful Math: daily lessons an adult teaches and grades. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review happen at every problem.
verdict: The Good and the Beautiful Math is a printed course of daily lessons. The adult teaches each lesson from a Course Book and grades the work from an answer key [1][2]. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous: every answer is checked and explained, updates the learner's level and sets the next problem.

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after updates the learner's level in that part of math and sets the next problem: new work within reach, a gap to close, or an old skill due back. The Good and the Beautiful Math starts a learner at one level with a placement test linked from each course page [1][2][3]. After that, the adult grades the work from an answer key [1].

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything a learner needs hangs off the problem in front of them: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a film where there is one, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. In The Good and the Beautiful Math the unit is the daily lesson. The Course Book is both the teacher's guide and the student book, and the adult leads each lesson with a Math Box of manipulatives and games [1][2]. In Math 6 and Pre-Algebra, videos are part of the course [3][4]. Across 55 studies, worked examples improve performance in math [9].

reasons.title: Feedback on every answer
reasons.body: After every answer AMP shows whether it was right, the correct answer and the worked steps, before the next problem. In The Good and the Beautiful Math the adult grades the work afterward from an answer key [1]. Pre-Algebra adds a manual with complete solutions [3]. Across 40 studies of computer feedback, feedback that explains had the largest average effect [8].

reasons.title: Moving on, and going back
reasons.body: In AMP an answer given after a hint or a lesson is marked as helped and does not count as learned. A skill counts when the learner gets it right without help, more than once, and repeated misses send practice back to what the skill builds on. In The Good and the Beautiful Math the next lesson is the next one in the book's order, and the adult sets the pace [1][2].

reasons.title: A level for each part of math
reasons.body: AMP keeps a separate level for each part of math, on one map of skills from counting through precalculus. A learner further along in geometry than in fractions gets work at both levels. The Good and the Beautiful Math places a learner in one level, a full-year course, and its math courses run from kindergarten to Pre-Algebra, called Level 8 [1][2][3][5].

rows.range: Kindergarten through Pre-Algebra, called Level 8. Each level is a full-year course [1][2][3][5].
rows.start: A placement test linked from each course page. The pages do not describe what it covers [1][2][3].
rows.teaching: The adult teaches from the Course Book with a Math Box of manipulatives and games [1][2]. Math 6 and Pre-Algebra add videos [3][4].
rows.next: The next lesson in the book's order. The adult sets the pace [1][2].
rows.mastery: None found in the pages we read [1][2][4].
rows.review: None found in the pages we read [1][2][4].
rows.print: Print is the course: full-color, wire-bound Course Books and answer keys, or PDFs. The same pages for every learner [1][2].
rows.adult: Teaches each lesson from the Course Book, runs the activities and games, and grades from the answer key [1][2].
rows.reports: None found in the pages we read [1]. The adult grades by hand [1].
rows.evidence: No outcome study found. As of November 2026, no entry in Evidence for ESSA and no What Works Clearinghouse intervention report [6][7]. Its math pages cite no research [2][4].

theirs: The Good and the Beautiful publishes homeschool curriculum in many subjects [5]. Its math line, Simply Good and Beautiful Math, runs from kindergarten through Level 7, then Pre-Algebra as Level 8 [3][5]. Each level is a full-year course [1][2].

A placement test sets the starting level [1][2][3]. The publisher describes a simple daily lesson format with activities and games, open and go [1]. The Course Book is both the teacher's guide and the student book: the adult leads each lesson, uses a Math Box of manipulatives, and grades from an answer key [1][2]. In Math 6 and Pre-Algebra, videos are part of the course, and Pre-Algebra has a manual with complete solutions [3][4].
credit: Hands-on math. Lessons use manipulatives, games and activities [1][2].
An adult teaches each lesson in person, from a book that is both guide and student book [1][2].
Pre-Algebra comes with complete written solutions [3].

theirs: We found no outcome study of The Good and the Beautiful Math on its math pages, in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports, as of November 2026 [2][4][6][7].
ours: Two findings bear on this comparison. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, feedback that explains had the largest average effect, 0.49, against 0.32 for the correct answer alone and 0.05 for right or wrong only [8]. These are averages by feedback type across mixed ages and subjects, not a head-to-head trial. Across 55 studies, worked examples improve performance in math, with an average effect of g = 0.48 [9]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and the code is public.

them: You want to teach each math lesson yourself at the table, with manipulatives and games.
amp: You want each answer checked and explained the moment it is given, with no pages to grade.
You want a hint, a lesson and the worked answer at every problem.
You want learned skills to keep coming back in practice.
Your learner is at different levels in different parts of math.
Your learner is finishing Pre-Algebra and wants algebra, geometry and precalculus next.

questions.question: How is AMP different from The Good and the Beautiful Math?
questions.answer: The Good and the Beautiful Math is daily lessons an adult teaches from a Course Book and grades from an answer key [1][2]. AMP has no separate test: every answer is checked, explained and sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does The Good and the Beautiful Math work?
questions.answer: We found no outcome study of it on its math pages, in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports, as of November 2026 [2][4][6][7].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. A learner can keep the Course Book for daily lessons and practice in AMP too. AMP places a learner from their first answers, whatever else they use.
